Content:
Let's now focus on the even case. What is the range of
[MATH: g(x) = -3\sqrt[4]{2x-1}-2?]

Content:
The range of [MATH: \sqrt[4] x] is
[MATH: \sqrt[4] x \ge 0.]

Content:
Now, let's apply transformations to the inequality above to turn the left-hand side into [MATH: g(x).]

Content:
First, remember that horizontal shifts and stretches do not affect the range. Therefore,
[MATH: \sqrt[4]{2x-1} \ge 0.]

Content:
Multiplying the above inequality by [MATH: -3] and then subtracting [MATH: 2,] we get

Content:
[MATH: root(2x − 1, 4)|≥ 0; − 3root(2x − 1, 4)|≤ 0; − 3root(2x − 1, 4) − 2|≤ − 2; g(x)|≤ − 2.]

Content:
Therefore, the range of the given function is [MATH: g(x) \in (-\infty,-2].]

Content:
We can also see that this is true from the graph of the function. The graph of [MATH: y=g(x)] is shown below.

Graphic:

Therefore, the range of the given function is [MATH: f(x) \in (-\infty,1].]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
The range of a radical function [MATH: f(x)=\sqrt[n]{x}] depends on whether the index [MATH: n] of the radical is even or odd.

Content:
Let's start with the odd case first. What is the range of [MATH: f(x) = -2\sqrt[3]{3x-2}+2?]

Content:
First, recall that the range of [MATH: y = \sqrt[3] x] is
[MATH: y \in (-\infty,\infty).]

Content:
Transformations do not change this interval. Therefore, the range of [MATH: f(x)] is [MATH: y \in (-\infty,\infty).]

Item 5 — Tutorial: The Range of a Transformed Radical Function With an Even Index

Content:
Let's now focus on the even case. What is the range of
[MATH: g(x) = -3\sqrt[4]{2x-1}-2?]

Content:
The range of [MATH: \sqrt[4] x] is
[MATH: \sqrt[4] x \ge 0.]

Content:
Now, let's apply transformations to the inequality above to turn the left-hand side into [MATH: g(x).]

Content:
First, remember that horizontal shifts and stretches do not affect the range. Therefore,
[MATH: \sqrt[4]{2x-1} \ge 0.]

Content:
Multiplying the above inequality by [MATH: -3] and then subtracting [MATH: 2,] we get

Content:
[MATH: root(2x − 1, 4)|≥ 0; − 3root(2x − 1, 4)|≤ 0; − 3root(2x − 1, 4) − 2|≤ − 2; g(x)|≤ − 2.]

Content:
Therefore, the range of the given function is [MATH: g(x) \in (-\infty,-2].]

Content:
We can also see that this is true from the graph of the function. The graph of [MATH: y=g(x)] is shown below.

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
The range of [MATH: \sqrt[4] x] is

[MATH: \sqrt[4] x \ge 0.]

Horizontal shifts and stretches do not affect the range. Therefore,

[MATH: \sqrt[4]{1-2x} \ge 0.]

Multiplying the above inequality by [MATH: -2] and then adding [MATH: 1,] we get

[MATH: root(1 − 2x, 4)|≥ 0; − 2root(1 − 2x, 4)|≤ 0; − 2root(1 − 2x, 4) + 1|≤ 1; f(x)|≤ 1.]

Therefore, the range of the given function is [MATH: f(x) \in (-\infty,1].]

We can also see that this is true from the graph of the function. The graph of [MATH: y=f(x)] is shown below.
